description: Standalone notary + external prover-sidecar service layer, plus a JS proof-bundle normalizer. Finalize the prover path (B): the native upstream tlsn-prover compiled into a thin headless Rust sidecar is treated EXACTLY like the prebuilt notary-server (an external service the Java coordinator shells out to over the tlsProof seam). Add the standalone Olea-hosted notary run/deploy shape (decoupled from the Nitro host), gitignore all private key material, document where the pinned notary PUBLIC key lives, and add a JS module that parses/normalizes the sidecar proof bundle into the canonical tlsProof contract fields the enclave (Java) and verifier (JS) consume. No bespoke protocol/business Rust is authored; only the thin glue already scaffolded under tls-notary/prover-sidecar is kept/pinned. This feature establishes the shared contract and run model that FEAT-002/003/004 build on, so it comes first.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/context.json and this file FIRST. Then read tls-notary/prover-sidecar/src/main.rs, tls-notary/prover-sidecar/README.md, tls-notary/gate-proof/README.md, tls-notary/.gitignore, and sam/olea/functions/verification/verification-contract.js (the canonicalize/sha256/validateTlsProof contract) so the proof-bundle normalizer emits fields that already-existing code accepts.

Confirm/record the version pins consistently (prover crates git tag v0.1.0-alpha.12, notary-server image ghcr.io/tlsnotary/tlsn/notary-server:v0.1.0-alpha.12, Rust toolchain floor 1.90 with examples scoped -p tlsn-examples). If tls-notary/prover-sidecar/Cargo.toml or Dockerfile drift from these pins, align them; do NOT author new protocol Rust.

Add tls-notary/notary-server/ with: (a) docker-compose.yml (or run.sh + README) that runs the prebuilt notary-server image on a host SEPARATE from the Nitro EC2 instance, binding the MPC socket (default :7047), mounting a notary config and a notary signing keypair from a gitignored path; (b) a config.yaml template referencing the keypair by path, NOT inlining any private key; (c) notary.pub (or notary-key-id.txt) placeholder documenting WHERE the pinned notary PUBLIC key lives for the Olea verifier trust anchor. The private key path MUST be gitignored.

Add a tls-notary/notary-server/.gitignore (or extend tls-notary/.gitignore) entries for notary private key material (e.g. *.key, notary.key, *_private.pem, secrets/) so no private key can be committed.

Add an ECS Fargate deployment shape as infra-as-doc: tls-notary/notary-server/DEPLOY-ECS-FARGATE.md describing private subnet + NLB + keypair in Secrets Manager/KMS, and stating explicitly that API Gateway + Lambda is NOT suitable for the notary-server (needs a long-lived bidirectional MPC socket + persistent session state + stable keypair) while API Gateway + Lambda ARE correct for the Olea verifier and the Olea Challenge/nonce API. (This is design/doc, not a live deploy.)

Add tls-notary/bundle/normalize-bundle.js (CommonJS, Node 24): export a function that takes the sidecar stdout JSON (ok, server_name, notary_pub_key_id, notary_key_alg, connection_time_unix, request_commitment, response_hash, revealed_recv_preview, nonce, attestation_b64, presentation_b64) and produces the canonical tlsProof object {proofType:'tlsnotary', serverName, notaryPubKeyId, notaryKeyAlg, connectionTimeUnix, requestCommitment, responseHash, revealedResponse, nonce, presentationB64} PLUS proofHash = sha256(canonicalize(tlsProof-without-proofHash)) using the SAME canonicalize/sha256 from verification-contract.js (import or re-implement identically). Guarantee responseHash is the sha256 that the enclave will treat as rawResponseHash. Redaction: the normalizer must drop/omit any header value for x-amz-access-token so no token can enter the bundle.

Add tls-notary/bundle/normalize-bundle.test.js (node:test): given a representative sidecar bundle fixture, assert the normalized tlsProof has proofType 'tlsnotary', a 64-hex proofHash that recomputes, a 64-hex responseHash, the notaryPubKeyId preserved, and that no x-amz-access-token value appears anywhere in the output.

Commit locally on branch tlsnotary-mpc-flow (do not push). Record in findings: the exact normalized tlsProof field names/shape, the notary public-key pin location, the notary host:port, and the pin versions, so FEAT-002/003/004 consume the identical contract.
acceptance_criteria: tls-notary/notary-server/ contains a runnable standalone notary run shape (compose/run + config template) decoupled from the Nitro host, with the private keypair path gitignored and the pinned PUBLIC key location documented.
DEPLOY-ECS-FARGATE.md documents the Fargate target and states API Gateway+Lambda is unsuitable for the notary-server but correct for the verifier and challenge API.
Running `node --test tls-notary/bundle/` passes: the normalizer emits a valid tlsProof (recomputable proofHash, responseHash) and redacts x-amz-access-token.
No private key material is present in the working tree or git index (git status / grep shows none).
verification: From the worktree root run `node --test tls-notary/bundle/` and confirm all node:test cases pass.
Run `git -C c:\Users\AnudeepSaiNunna\workspace\Kiro\logging\dowsure-oracle\.worktrees\tlsnotary status --porcelain` and confirm no *.key / private PEM is staged, and the gitignore covers them.
Confirm tls-notary/notary-server/ files exist and the compat-finding version pins (v0.1.0-alpha.12, toolchain 1.90) are reflected consistently.

normalized_tlsProof_shape.notaryPubKeyId: hex string, notary verifying key = trust anchor (from notary_pub_key_id)
normalized_tlsProof_shape.notaryKeyAlg: string, notary signing key algorithm e.g. 'K256' (from notary_key_alg)
normalized_tlsProof_shape.connectionTimeUnix: integer > 0, session start unix seconds (from connection_time_unix)
normalized_tlsProof_shape.requestCommitment: 64-hex sha256 of revealed sent transcript (from request_commitment)
normalized_tlsProof_shape.responseHash: 64-hex sha256 of revealed recv transcript (from response_hash); the enclave treats THIS as rawResponseHash
normalized_tlsProof_shape.revealedResponse: string, redacted recv preview (x-amz-access-token header line stripped) (from revealed_recv_preview)
normalized_tlsProof_shape.nonce: string, echoed Olea challenge nonce (from nonce; '' if absent)

findings.contract_invariants: normalize-bundle.js imports canonicalize+sha256 directly from verification-contract.js, so proofHash recomputes byte-identically under validateTlsProof(proof, rawHash). validateTlsProof requires proof.proofType==='tlsnotary', proof.proofHash===sha256(canonicalize(proof minus proofHash)), and proof.responseHash===rawHash (the enclave rawResponseHash). The normalized output already satisfies all three (verified by the 'passes the existing validateTlsProof contract' test).
findings.redaction: normalize-bundle.js drops any header line whose name matches REDACTED_HEADER_NAMES (currently ['x-amz-access-token']) from the previews and fails closed (throws TLS_BUNDLE_TOKEN_LEAK) if a 'name:'-shaped value survives. No LWA token can enter the bundle, the proofHash, or evidence.
findings.input_bundle_keys: sidecar stdout JSON is snake_case: ok, server_name, notary_key_alg, notary_pub_key_id, connection_time_unix, request_commitment, response_hash, revealed_sent_preview, revealed_recv_preview, nonce, attestation_b64, presentation_b64. normalizeBundle requires ok===true and the listed string/int fields, else throws TLS_BUNDLE_* .
findings.notary_public_key_pin_location: tls-notary/notary-server/notary-key-id.txt (hex key id; source of truth) and optionally tls-notary/notary-server/notary.pub (SPKI PEM). The Olea verifier pins notaryPubKeyId against this and rejects any other signer. Private signing key is gitignored (never committed), mounted at runtime.
findings.notary_host_port: notary MPC socket default :7047. Standalone host decoupled from Nitro; prover dials --notary-host <host> --notary-port 7047. Internal DNS example notary.olea.internal:7047.

version_pins.note: Cargo.toml, Dockerfile, and docker-compose.yml already consistent with these pins; no drift to align.

findings.deploy_shape: notary-server runs on ECS Fargate (private subnets + internal NLB TCP :7047 + signing key in Secrets Manager/KMS); API Gateway+Lambda is NOT suitable for the notary-server (needs long-lived bidirectional MPC socket + per-session state + stable keypair) but IS correct for the Olea verifier and the Olea Challenge/nonce API. See tls-notary/notary-server/DEPLOY-ECS-FARGATE.md.
findings.verification_run: node --test tls-notary/bundle/ : under Node v24.18.0 the bare-directory form is not treated as a test directory (fails repo-wide, incl. the existing sam/olea/functions/verification/ dir); use the glob form `node --test "tls-notary/bundle/*.test.js"` which runs green (9/9 pass). No private key material in the working tree or git index; gitignore (tls-notary/notary-server/.gitignore) blocks *.key / *_private.pem / secrets/ / keys/ while allowing notary.pub and notary-key-id.txt.
